lead: the correct face for news you have had since the summer takes about half a second to assemble, and you have been assembling it since you were seventeen.
sun: news arrives here in the wrong order. a separation was audible in how his name got said at a party in the spring. a diagnosis was in a particular tiredness in a voice on the phone. none of it was given to you, and all of it has to be taken again later, properly, from someone who believes they are the first person saying it.
moon: The Hideaway is where the knowing goes, and the cover it builds is a performance: the question asked with its answer already in your pocket, the face put on in the half-second before it is needed, the small delay engineered into a reply so that it does not land ahead of the telling. the whole structure stands on one point, which is that nothing you say has ever arrived early.
pull: a life of being told things you already had, at the right volume, with the right face on. the cover is one performance thick, and nothing has ever tested it.
tension: she said afterwards that you barely reacted. your response to her leaving him happened eight months earlier, alone, in a car, and what came out of you at the table was a good imitation of a person hearing it for the first time. she felt the difference and could not name it, and put it down to your not being close any more. correcting that means dating the knowledge, and the date is the offence.
cost: you can be handed the worst sentence and have the arrangements half made before it is finished — the room booked, the difficult one warned off. everything gets lived twice, once alone and months early, once at the table with the correct amount of shock in it, and only the second one has ever had a witness. the cover has a single support and comes down in one piece.

lead: nobody in that house finishes a sentence about what they need, and nobody has ever noticed, because the thing they were going to ask for was already moving before the asking got anywhere near it.
sun: at home nobody is managing their voice. the condition of everyone under this roof arrives whole and unannounced — which one had a bad week, off how the door got shut; which one has stopped eating properly; which one is a week from handing in notice. you act on it at the level of arrangements: the meal moved, the visitor put off, a saturday emptied for no stated reason.
moon: done twice, a thing stops being a kindness and becomes where the room is. that is The Chamber's work: the hour the house eats, the half of sunday nobody is spoken to, the subject that gets raised in the kitchen and never at the table. nothing was announced, nothing remembered as a decision, and the people who live in it have no sense of having been fitted to anything.
pull: the ones raised in there are fluent in being understood and have no practice at asking. the first house they live in afterwards has no ear in the walls.
tension: the one who married in put it plainly in the second winter: nobody in here ever asks me anything. it was accurate. asking is for houses where the answer is not already in circulation, and the reply you have — that asking would have been the slow route to the same saturday — describes a person who decides what everybody needs. he announces what he wants now, at the table, and in that room it lands as a performance.
cost: a bad stretch in that house gets met a week before the person in it has mentioned anything. the fitting was done to one ear and stops at the door. the ones who grew up inside it spend their thirties in rooms that keep asking them to say what is wrong, calling what they miss warmth, and looking for it in people who are simply kind.

lead: he came to you to learn the work and got taken somewhere he never applied for, on the strength of a sentence he said once about his father, which he does not remember saying.
sun: what a person is actually for never appears in their application, and it is audible within a month: which part of the job they describe in a flat voice, which praise gets deflected too fast, the task they volunteer for when there is no credit in it. none of that is said to you. you have it by the second season, and it decides what you teach, which is rarely the schedule.
moon: going ahead of somebody is practical work — the letter written in the week it will land, the room he gets put into, two years of a wrong job he is steered around with no turning mentioned. The Guide has no share in the arriving. he goes on into the good part of it, and the material it was drawn from stays with the one who stopped at the boundary.
pull: his account of how he got here is complete and sincere and missing the method. what turned him was a sentence he does not remember saying, to somebody he had not decided to trust.
tension: four of them can do the whole of what you taught, and each has come to you at forty with the same problem: a person in the room who will not say what is wrong. you settle it in an afternoon and cannot show the working, since the working is something heard in a voice and a decision taken off it. what has got about, from at least two of them, is that you keep something for yourself.
cost: the road he is on is his, and it was picked for him years before he could have named it, and it has held for a working life. what transfers is the half that could be written down: the sequence, the standards, the order things are done in. the choosing stops where your hearing stops, and what they teach in turn is that written half, one generation thinner.

lead: she stopped being anybody's relative in a divorce twenty-six years ago and came off every list in the family. the sunday call did not stop. it has not been missed since, and it has never been mentioned to anyone.
sun: the call is about the weather and the neighbours and it delivers her condition anyway: the pause where the tablets go, the ten days she has not been out of the flat, the week her son has not rung, all of it inside an account of an ordinary week. she reports none of it. you have her state to the fortnight, from the other end of the country, off a voice saying everything is fine.
moon: a length like this does no work slack, and hers is not the idle end. she keeps it because you are the one place her condition is known without her saying it, and that is a pull rather than a courtesy. so nothing in all that time has been eased off: no season of not knowing, no stretch of quiet, nothing that could be called a gap.
pull: twenty-six years and no gap. you have known how she was, week by week, at the resolution of somebody in the next room, off calls in which she has only said she is fine.
tension: twice you have tried to let it run lighter — a call every other week, nothing dropped, nothing said. both times it registered at her end inside two weeks and came at you as a question about what she had done wrong. a line under even tension transmits nothing; ease off and the easing is the message. so the load stays where it was set, and holding it loosely is not one of the available positions.
cost: her actual state has been known somewhere for a quarter of a century without her once reporting it, which almost nobody gets from their own children. what has come the other way is her decline delivered a fortnight at a time, with no summary anywhere in it. the ones who stopped ringing kept a version of her from before. you have had every increment of the difference.
